survey: A cartoon rocket floating against a blue sunburst, leaning slightly so its nose points up and to the right. The red nose cone sits on a silver cylindrical body, and a red collar ring marks the joint. Two round portholes with copper rims sit one above the other near the front center of the body. Their line tilts with the rocket's axis. Two red fins come off the left and right sides of the lower body. Because they stick out sideways, their flat sides face the camera, and each shows a narrow top edge, as you'd expect from a slightly high camera. At the base is a black nozzle band with a small yellow flame coming out of it, offset along the axis. The collar ring and the nozzle band both curve downward in the middle, so both are seen from slightly above. Both rings dip to the right, which matches the lean of the axis, and that tilt also explains why the right fin attaches lower than the left. The portholes face the camera almost straight on, so drawing them as near-circles is fine at this angle. There is no ground plane. The whole object is seen from one consistent slightly-high three-quarter view.
